chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abī al-Faḍl, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Jamīl, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about al-Jumuʿah during travel: what should I recite in them both? He said:
Recite in them both: Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad.

So in this report he permitted the recitation of Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad, while in the report it states that he repeats, whether he was in travel or in residence. Thus, if what was intended were other than what we have mentioned of encouragement, he would not have allowed that for him.

key_terms.اقْرَأْ: recite; the Imam’s directive regarding what to read in prayer
key_terms.التَّرْغِيبِ: encouragement or recommendation inferred from the wording
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which the ruling is being asked about
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: the Jumuʿah prayer discussed in the report
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or narration under discussion
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, specified here as the recitation
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats; indicating repetition mentioned in another report

ai.seo_question: What should be recited in Jumuʿah prayer while traveling according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the recitation in the prayer of Jumuʿah while traveling, stating that Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ may be recited in both rakʿahs. The closing note clarifies that this permission is understood as a form of allowance and encouragement, within the broader jurisprudential discussion on the preferred recitation for Jumuʿah prayer.
